chronology: [Backstory] Steelhead saves the female twin of dying Dona Vicenta by transplanting the male twin's brain into the girl's body; the male body is preserved in stasis.
[Backstory] Aghora is raised as male heir, tames the Tarantuwolf Deyanira at age five, and undergoes Metabaron initiation including bionic hand replacement.
[Backstory] Aghora serves as executioner on prison planet Khaliyuga; Steelhead, grief-stricken, replaces his flesh with Storlon.
[Backstory] Aghora seals Steelhead in a stasis cocoon and ejects him into deep space after she cannot kill him in combat.
[Backstory] Aghora waits three years for an Imperial assignment; Mirror Ships of an alien race devastate the Imperial Fleet; the Empire still does not summon her.
Aghora travels to the Golden Planet to learn why the Metabaron has not been called.
The Imperial court debates surrender; a bald false Metabaron arrives on a giant spider mount, is denounced as inauthentic, and expelled.
Aghora confronts the court; the crowd discovers she is a woman and turns violent; she purges the court, killing many.
The Emperor meets Aghora, offers her command of the Imperial Fleet; she refuses and demands massive payment in kublars to fight alone.
Robots Lothar and Tonto bicker; Lothar combusts from lust for Aghora, is repaired, and apologizes.
Aghora uses the mirror principle and an invisibility cloak to penetrate the enemy screen at hyper-light speed.
Aghora reaches the far ends of the universe, bypasses paleo-jellyfish, and targets their controlling source.
Applying Bushitaka's doctrine, Aghora fires a precision laser to sever the enemy mother-brain's pineal gland.
An exact physical duplicate of Aghora confronts her in space; she defeats and dissolves it by asserting her soul cannot be copied.
Aghora destroys a cosmically connected entity despite its surrender plea; a Metabaron-aligned voice invokes the code of victory or death.
The interdimensional gateway closes; the invading jellyfish lose their energy source and dissolve; Aghora leaves the universe.
Aghora is awarded the empire's highest honor, the pluri-galactic medallion, by the Technopope before the galactic senate on the Golden Planet.
Deyanira the Tarantuwolf rampages during the ceremony, killing the Technopope; Aghora subdues her nonlethally and returns to the Metabunker.
Tonto diagnoses Deyanira with a terminal tumor; Aghora resolves to euthanize her; Deyanira gives a final affectionate lick.
Deyanira's remains are ejected into space via a Paleo-Viking funerary ritual; Aghora sheds her first tear.
Grieving and despairing over her capacity only to kill, Aghora resolves to have a child.
The stasis-preserved male twin's body is removed and immediately decomposes, eliminating it as a source of male cells.
Aghora uses hypo-genetics to extract tissue from her own male brain matter and self-conceives—the first auto-conception in history.
Pregnant, Aghora retreats in secret to the garden planet Flos to give birth away from civilization.
[Teaser] Next episode: 'The Return of the Shabda-Oud.'
locations: Golden Planet (seat of the galactic senate and Imperial court)
Imperial throne room and ceremonial hall
The Metabunker (Aghora's base, with medical and diagnostic facilities)
Outer space battlefield around Imperial ships
Enemy territory at the far ends of the universe (organic-mechanical corridors, paleo-jellyfish environment)
Interdimensional gateway site where dwellers from another dimension entered this universe
Open space near a large planetary body (site of the mirror-duplicate combat)
Garden planet Flos (peaceful refuge where Aghora retreats pregnant)
lore_laws: Metabaron succession traditionally passes from father to son.
A Metabaron's sworn word is treated as an absolute and solemn commitment.
The Metabaron code permits only victory or death; surrender or mercy is explicitly rejected.
Storlon is described as an indestructible metal.
Mirror Ships reflect every attack back at the attacker; their weakness is having that reflected force turned against them.
A psycho-mimetic aura enables stealth and passage through defensive screens.
Bushitaka's combat doctrine: defeat an overwhelmingly large enemy by severing its equivalent of the head rather than engaging it directly.
A body preserved in stasis decomposes immediately upon removal from the stasis chamber.
Hypo-genetics can transform brain tissue into viable sperm cells, enabling self-conception.
Kublars are a currency unit used for military contracting.
The empire's highest individual honor is the pluri-galactic medallion, conferred by the Technopope.
The galactic senate convenes on the Golden Planet; major imperial factions include the Empress, Imperial Court, Endoguard, Techno-Techno Guild, Ekonomat, and the army.
Invading jellyfish from another dimension depend on an energy source tied to their interdimensional gateway; closing the gateway dissolves them.
major_events: Mirror Ships of an alien race obliterate the Imperial Fleet, threatening all galaxies in the universe.
A bald false Metabaron arrives on a giant spider mount, is denounced as inauthentic, and expelled from the Imperial court.
Aghora purges the Imperial court and negotiates a solo contract with the Emperor, refusing command of the fleet.
Aghora infiltrates enemy space using the mirror principle and an invisibility cloak, then destroys the enemy mother-brain with a precision laser following Bushitaka's decapitation doctrine.
Aghora defeats her own mirror duplicate in single combat, proving her soul cannot be physically replicated.
Aghora destroys a cosmically connected entity; the interdimensional gateway closes and the invading jellyfish dissolve, ending the invasion.
Aghora is publicly awarded the pluri-galactic medallion before the galactic senate.
Deyanira the Tarantuwolf kills the Technopope during the award ceremony; Aghora subdues and later euthanizes her dying companion.
Grieving Deyanira's death, Aghora performs the first auto-conception in history via hypo-genetics and retreats pregnant to the garden planet Flos.
open_uncertainties: The identity of the bald false Metabaron who arrives on a giant spider mount and is expelled from the Imperial court is never named in these pages.
Whether the crowd-assault scene on p03 depicts Deyanira the person or another figure is not fully explicit.
The exact nature of the psycho-mimetic aura—whether it is a suit function, innate ability, or separate device—is not explained.
The identity of the cosmically connected entity Aghora destroys, and the precise anatomy of the enemy mother-brain, remain visually ambiguous.
The gold-faced armored figure present during the space battle sequence (p06) is not named.
Whether 'Aghora' and 'Agohra' used across pages represent a single spelling or two distinct characters is unclear from the images alone.
The close-up cybernetic face during the gateway confrontation spread (p13-p14) is not explicitly identified.
Exact wording of several key dialogues is uncertain throughout due to image-resolution limitations noted across multiple pages.
recurring_motifs: Mirror and reflection as weapon, barrier, and philosophical problem: attacks reflected back, a physical duplicate grown, a mirror barrier breached
Body modification and transgression of biological limits: brain transplant, bionic limbs, Storlon flesh replacement, self-conception from brain tissue
Soul versus body: physical copying is shown as insufficient to reproduce inner essence or identity
Grief and loss triggering decisive transformation: Steelhead replacing his flesh, Aghora shedding her first tear, Aghora's decision to create life
The Metabaron's radical self-sufficiency: refusing fleet command, fighting alone, reproducing without a partner
Biomechanical aesthetics: dense tubing, spider-like mounts, jellyfish entities, organic-mechanical corridors throughout
Legitimacy and succession: who truly qualifies as a Metabaron is contested multiple times across the volume
title: The Mirror Effect
